boundary_rationale: The row opens at the frame header, הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֣ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ (oshb:Jer.7.1, byte tier) — ‘hadavar asher hayah el-Yirmeyahu,’ ‘the word that came to Jeremiah’ — the prose-sermon superscription shape that opens this collection. The command to stand at the gate and proclaim (web:Jer.7.2) introduces quoted content that itself opens with the title-stack formula כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Jer.7.3, byte tier) at 7.3, argues from covenant obedience through the Decalogue-echoing charges of 7.9, “Will you steal, murder, commit adultery, swear falsely, burn incense to Baal” (web:Jer.7.9), and turns on the Shiloh precedent at 7.12, אֶל מְקוֹמִי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּשִׁיל֔וֹ (oshb:Jer.7.12, byte tier) — spelled בשילו here, one of three forms the place-name takes at its several sites in the book. Yahweh remains the speaker and the people, through Jeremiah, the addressee from 7.3 through the closing threat, “I will cast you out of my sight, as I have cast out all your brothers” (web:Jer.7.15). The row ends there because 7.16 turns the address to the prophet himself in direct second-person prohibition, a discourse-frame imperative that opens a fresh unit.

boundary_rationale: The row opens on a direct second-person prohibition, וְאַתָּ֞ה אַל תִּתְפַּלֵּ֣ל בְּעַד הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֗ה (oshb:Jer.7.16, byte tier) — ‘ve-attah al-titpallel be'ad ha-am ha-zeh,’ ‘and you, do not pray for this people’ — turning the address from the people back to the prophet himself, a discourse-frame imperative distinct from the temple-gate proclamation before it. The forbidden intercession is grounded in the offerings to the “queen of the sky” described at 7.18, the women knead the dough, to make cakes to the queen of the sky (web:Jer.7.18), and the unit closes on the consequence clause לָכֵ֞ן כֹּה אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֗ה (oshb:Jer.7.20, byte tier) — ‘lachen koh amar Adonai YHWH,’ ‘therefore thus says the Lord Yahweh’ — which keeps the same speaker and the same referent, ‘this place,’ as the prohibition rather than opening a fresh address; the koh-amar formula here marks emphasis, not a change of whose mouth speaks.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The therefore-clause at 7.20 could open its own row as a fresh koh-amar onset, but it continues the same divine speaker and the same topic as 7.16-19 rather than naming a new addressee or scene, so the consequence is kept inside the prohibition unit rather than split from it.

strongest_rejected_alternative: The renewed commission at 7.27 could open its own row as a fresh address to the prophet, paralleling 7.16, but its topic still belongs to the sacrifice-critique already under way rather than a different subject, so it is kept as the unit's closing move rather than a fresh frame.

The recurring judgment formula at 7.32, לָכֵ֞ן הִנֵּֽה יָמִ֤ים בָּאִים֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.7.32, byte tier) — ‘lachen hineh yamim ba'im, ne'um YHWH,’ ‘therefore behold, the days come, says Yahweh’ — turns the Topheth renaming toward a burial shortage, “The dead bodies of this people will be food for the birds of the sky” (web:Jer.7.33), that the 8.1 scene continues without a fresh word-event or date frame: בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֣יא נְאֻם יְהוָ֡ה (oshb:Jer.8.1, byte tier, a verse carrying its own ketiv/qere note) — ‘ba'et ha-hi, ne'um YHWH,’ ‘at that time, declares Yahweh’ — extends the same no-burial judgment to the exhumed bones of kings, priests, and prophets, “They will not be gathered or be buried. They will be like dung on the surface of the earth” (web:Jer.8.2). The row closes at 8.3 because 8.4 opens a fresh commission to the prophet with its own koh-amar formula.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The Topheth judgment (7.30-34) and the bone-exhumation scene (8.1-3) could split at the chapter break, but both develop the same burial-denial threat opened by the mourning command, so the chapter division is not read as a unit boundary here.

device_notes: The content is a wisdom aphorism about the ground of legitimate boasting rather than an announcement of judgment or salvation; it is carried under the judgment-oracle heading as a stand-in for a koh-amar-framed prophetic saying, since the controlled vocabulary does not include a dedicated wisdom-saying type. A setumah opens the row at oshb:Jer.9.21, immediately before it, and another closes it at oshb:Jer.9.23 (single-witness, WLC).

boundary_rationale: The row opens on the recurring judgment formula, oshb:Jer.9.24 = web:Jer.9.25, הִנֵּ֛ה יָמִ֥ים בָּאִ֖ים נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.9.24, byte tier) — ‘hineh yamim ba'im, ne'um YHWH,’ ‘behold, the days come, says Yahweh’ — the same shape that opened the Topheth threat earlier in this stretch (web:Jer.7.32), now opening a circumcision oracle. The nation roster, oshb:Jer.9.25 = web:Jer.9.26, עַל מִצְרַ֣יִם וְעַל יְהוּדָ֗ה וְעַל אֱד֞וֹם (oshb:Jer.9.25, byte tier) — naming Egypt, Judah, and Edom beside “all who have the corners of their hair cut off, who dwell in the wilderness” (web:Jer.9.26), closes on the verdict, כִּ֤י כָל הַגּוֹיִם֙ עֲרֵלִ֔ים וְכָל בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עַרְלֵי לֵֽב (oshb:Jer.9.25, byte tier) — ‘ki khol ha-goyim arelim ve-khol beit Yisrael arlei lev,’ ‘for all the nations are uncircumcised, and all the house of Israel is uncircumcised in heart.’ The row and the part both end at 9.26.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The nation roster and its verdict (9.26) could be split into two short rows at the list-to-verdict turn, but the roster serves the verdict that closes the same sentence rather than standing as independent content, so they are kept as one unit.
